ul-4-097.title: The Heavy Tomes
ul-4-097.text: Thick calfskin volumes settle with a sodden thud into the black channel, their gold-leafed spines absorbing the dark liquor of the tributary feeder. You wedge the massive encyclopedias between two trembling iron pillars, diverting the greasy current into a temporary backwater where the surface skims clear. Carefully, you press sheets of dry blotting paper across the damp flagstones, soaking up the residual sheen until the slate is workable. The lamp-oil gutters low in your brass lantern, casting long, wavering shadows against the towering stacks of forgotten geography.
exits: Step across the dry stone path

ul-4-098.title: The Dammed Rill
ul-4-098.text: Heavy iron-clasped geographies serve as your temporary masonry, dropped one by one into the pulsing throat of the feeder until the black fluid slows to a sluggish trickle. You work with frantic haste, your fingers stained deep with walnut-brown gall, stacking damp folios to block every escaping rivulet. Across the makeshift timber-and-paper barrier, a pocket of clean air opens above a dry stretch of flooring. You slide your remaining stack of blotting paper into the sheltered recess, keeping the fragile sheets safe from the drifting spray.

ul-4-099.title: Choking the Sluice
ul-4-099.text: Swelling pressure from the upstream feeder threatens to blow your hasty dam apart as black fluid bubbles furiously around the edges of the heavy encyclopedias. You throw your full weight against the spine of a massive biographical dictionary, trying to wedge it deeper into the groove before the entire barricade gives way under the rising tide. The soaked paper groans and slips beneath your palms, threatening to burst the seal and wash your dry cache into the void.

ul-4-100.title: Soaking the Stash
ul-4-100.text: A sudden surge of black liquor punches right through the center of your barricade, showering your boots and clothes in bitter, staining sludge. The precious cache of dry blotting paper drinks the overflow in an instant, swelling into a useless, soggy pulp that falls apart in your hands. You scramble backward up the slippery stone slope, coughing against the sharp smell of iron gall and lamp-oil, poorer by a dozen sheets and half your breath.

ul-4-101.title: The Sluice Dam
ul-4-101.text:
Heavy calfskin encyclopedias tumble into the tributary feeder one by one, their dense paper absorbing the black current until the trickling water pools and stalls. You scoop up a thick bundle of dry blotting paper from the ledge before the pressure shifts, stuffing the absorbent sheets into your coat pocket where they will keep damp ink at bay for hours to come.

This salvaged stack-guard's paper remains stiff and dry, ready to soak up stray fluids or shield your fingers from biting bindings in the deeper vaults.
exits: Retrace your steps toward the sluice

ul-4-102.title: The Ferryman's Toll
ul-4-102.text: A flat-bottomed punt drifts out from the shadow of the iron stacks, poled by a silent figure draped in grease-stained canvas. You reach into your pocket and draw out a twisted pinch of coarse grey salt, holding it flat upon your palm until the rower's dark eyes catch the glint of mineral. A gnarled hand reaches across the gunwale to accept the trade, dropping a small notched bone disc into your palm in return.

ul-4-103.title: Bargaining in Ink
ul-4-103.text: The hooded rower pauses his long ash pole inches from the stone shelf, watching you with the suspicious stillness of a gargoyle. You offer the pinch of grey salt across the dark gap, pitching your voice to a low, respectful murmur that will not disturb the whispering margins around you. The ferryman cocks his head, weighing your sincerity against the rising tide of the ink-rivers below.

ul-4-104.title: A Sour Trade
ul-4-104.text: Your hand slips on the damp stone as you reach out, spilling half the precious salt into the dark current where it dissolves in an instant. The rower scowls, a harsh sound like dry parchment tearing, and pushes the punt an arm's length away from the ledge. You are left standing alone with wet boots and a lighter pouch, forced to find another way across the channel without a token.

ul-4-105.title: The Ferry Token
ul-4-105.text:
A pinch of coarse grey salt drawn from your provisions draws a low, rasping whistle from the hooded ink-rower, who steers his skiff against the drifting current long enough for you to step aboard the damp timber planks. He drops a heavy, cold disk of cast lead into your palm before pushing off into the gloom, a small circular assurance of safe passage across any dark water in the stacks.

This notched ferry token hums faintly against your thumb, promising another crossing whenever the channels block your path.
exits: Return toward the waste ink sluice

ul-4-106.title: The Iron Trial
ul-4-106.text: Heavy iron doors stand ajar within the deepest roots of the annexe, revealing a succession of vaulted chambers where the history of the Underlibrary sits in silent judgment. Every stone surface is carved with ancient administrative verdicts, echoing softly with the voices of forgotten cataloguers who weighed the worth of every manuscript ever shelved. You step across the threshold into the chill draft of the tribunal, feeling the weight of centuries pressing against your conscience. The walls themselves seem to watch you, noting every hesitation as you search for any trace of Thessaly Marr among the dusty records.
exits: Enter the court of red ink
